headline.caveat: 5-year AI cloud contract: Microsoft buys GPU-cloud capacity on NVIDIA GB300s at IREN's Childress, TX campus (750MW site; ~200MW dedicated).

realized_to_date.caveat: Microsoft made a ~20% prepayment (~$1.9B, press-reported) at signing; service revenue ramps through 2026 as GB300 phases energize.

nature_md: Microsoft contracted ~$9.7B over five years of GPU-as-a-service capacity from IREN on NVIDIA GB300 systems at Childress, Texas, with a ~20% prepayment. IREN — a bitcoin miner turned vertically-integrated AI cloud — bought ~$5.8B of GB300 systems from Dell to serve the contract (see related edge). Microsoft rents rather than builds: faster time-to-compute at the cost of margin and a new counterparty dependence. Capacity phases in through 2026-27.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Microsoft books the prepayment as a contract asset/prepaid expense amortized against usage; ongoing payments are cost of revenue for Azure/AI services. The 5-year commitment appears in purchase obligations.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: IREN recognizes cloud-services revenue over the term (deferred revenue from the prepayment), against heavy upfront Dell capex — a working-capital structure where the customer's prepayment part-funds the hardware that serves it.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** IREN converts power assets into a five-year investment-grade revenue stream at cloud margins, prepaid. **Bear:** one customer is most of IREN's forward revenue; the $5.8B hardware bet has GB300-generation obsolescence risk if Microsoft doesn't renew in 2030.
